title: New Horizons in Carbohydrate Research and Application for Endurance Athletes
population: Endurance athletes; contemporary review of carbohydrate research and application
findings: High carbohydrate availability for prolonged intense exercise and competition remains a priority.
Recent advances on the recommended type and quantity of carbohydrate before, during and after intense bouts.

The contemporary view of 'train-low' based on the totality of evidence suggests limited utility for enhancing performance benefits from training, but periodising carbohydrate intake to the goal and demand of training or competition is important.
Calls for a more personalised approach to carbohydrate recommendations, potentially supported by continuous glucose monitoring.
limitations: Narrative review; abstract gives no numeric dose recommendations and full text was not read.
implications: Periodise carbohydrate: high availability around key long or intense sessions and races.
Do not schedule train-low as a performance enhancer; at most an optional, rare, low-intensity adaptation tool.
Fuelling module should allow athlete-specific tolerance data to personalise targets.

verification.notes: Crossref match; findings paraphrase the Europe PMC abstract only.
